documents.title: Synthetic Alder: unfinished handoffs
documents.text: Current validated rule for the fictional Alder project: when a worker leaves with an unfinished assignment, record the last completed action and the next executable action together in a handoff capsule. This rule concerns interrupted work, not finished assignments.

documents.title: Synthetic Alder: completed handoffs
documents.text: Current validated rule for the fictional Alder project: after an assignment is finished, place its final deliverable and acceptance receipt in a closure capsule. There is no next executable action in a closure capsule.

documents.title: Synthetic Alder: retired interruption practice
documents.text: Historical rule for the fictional Alder project: an interrupted worker should leave only its last completed action. This was replaced by the handoff capsule rule requiring both the last action and the next executable action; it must not guide current work.

documents.title: Synthetic Brindle: duplicate work packets
documents.text: Current validated procedure for the fictional Brindle project: packets with the same payload fingerprint are consolidated into one work item even if their arrival times differ. Preserve all sender receipts on the consolidated item. Payload identity, not arrival time, defines duplicate work.

documents.title: Synthetic Brindle: simultaneous packets
documents.text: Current validated procedure for the fictional Brindle project: packets arriving at the same instant but carrying different payload fingerprints remain separate work items. Arrival-time equality alone cannot justify consolidation.

documents.title: Synthetic Brindle: rejected identity shortcut
documents.text: Rejected proposal for the fictional Brindle project: treat all packets arriving in the same time slot as duplicates regardless of content. The synthetic review found that this merged distinct assignments. This proposal provides no current support for consolidation.

documents.title: Synthetic Cobalt: ambiguous routing
documents.text: Current validated rule for the fictional Cobalt project: if two routing labels are equally supported, hold the item in the ambiguity tray and request a discriminator. Do not choose either destination while the tie persists.

documents.title: Synthetic Cobalt: missing routing information
documents.text: Current validated rule for the fictional Cobalt project: if an item has no routing label at all, send it to the intake desk for initial classification. The intake desk handles missing evidence, not a tie between supported labels.

documents.title: Synthetic Cobalt: outside routing suggestion
documents.text: Unreviewed external suggestion for the fictional Cobalt project: when two routing labels tie, pick the shorter label. This suggestion has not been accepted and is not evidence for the current routing procedure.

documents.title: Synthetic Dapple: archived receipt retrieval
documents.text: The current validated lookup procedure in the fictional Dapple project is identified as KITE-731-Q. Given an archived receipt's stable handle, open the original receipt and verify its content seal before quoting it. This procedure retrieves existing receipts; it does not issue new ones.

documents.title: Synthetic Dapple: new receipt issuance
documents.text: The current validated issuance procedure in the fictional Dapple project is identified as KITE-731-R. For a newly accepted delivery, mint a receipt handle and compute its initial content seal. It does not describe checking an archived receipt before quotation.

documents.title: Synthetic Ember: participant cancellation
documents.text: Current validated rule in the fictional Ember project: if a participant cancels a reserved session, release the seat immediately and retain a cancellation receipt. This rule applies to an explicit cancellation before the session starts.

documents.title: Synthetic Ember: participant nonattendance
documents.text: Current validated rule in the fictional Ember project: if a participant neither cancels nor attends, keep the seat reserved until the session begins, then mark the reservation as unattended. Nonattendance does not trigger an advance seat release.

documents.title: Synthetic Ember: retired cancellation delay
documents.text: Historical procedure in the fictional Ember project held an explicitly cancelled seat until the session began. The validated immediate-release rule supersedes this procedure. It is no longer an acceptable basis for handling cancellations.

documents.title: Synthetic Fallow: conflict between copies
documents.text: Current validated rule for the fictional Fallow project: when a generated summary contradicts its underlying signed note, use the signed note and regenerate the summary. The note is authoritative; the summary is a replaceable derivative.

documents.title: Synthetic Fallow: conflict between signed notes
documents.text: Current validated rule for the fictional Fallow project: if two signed notes disagree and neither supersedes the other, mark the claim unresolved and ask for adjudication. This is a dispute between authoritative records, not a summary-generation error.

documents.title: Synthetic Fallow: rejected recency heuristic
documents.text: Rejected proposal for the fictional Fallow project: resolve every disagreement by selecting the file with the newest modification time, including generated summaries. The proposal was refuted in the synthetic review and cannot establish which content is authoritative.

documents.title: Synthetic Glade: restart after temporary outage
documents.text: Current validated procedure MOSS/42:RESUME in the fictional Glade project restarts a paused delivery after a temporary outage. Resume from the last acknowledged parcel and do not resend earlier acknowledged parcels. The recipient and destination must remain unchanged.

documents.title: Synthetic Glade: destination replacement
documents.text: Current validated procedure MOSS/42:REDIRECT in the fictional Glade project handles a changed destination. Start a new delivery record linked to the prior record and confirm the new recipient. It is not the temporary-outage restart procedure.

documents.title: Synthetic Harbor: publication embargo
documents.text: Current validated policy in the fictional Harbor project: a fully approved packet with a future release date stays in the embargo cabinet until that date. Approval is complete; timing alone prevents publication.

documents.title: Synthetic Harbor: publication review pending
documents.text: Current validated policy in the fictional Harbor project: a packet whose approval is incomplete stays in the review cabinet, even if its intended release date has passed. Pending approval, rather than an embargo, prevents publication.

documents.title: Synthetic Harbor: abandoned early-release idea
documents.text: Unreviewed outside idea for the fictional Harbor project: release approved packets immediately even when they carry a future release date. It has no authorization and must not be treated as the current publication policy.

documents.title: Synthetic Iris: reversible labeling trial
documents.text: Current validated trial plan VELA_208-B in the fictional Iris project tests new shelf labels using removable sleeves on a duplicate shelf. The trial cannot alter the primary collection. Success is judged by the synthetic trial's predefined label-matching task.

documents.title: Synthetic Iris: accepted label rollout
documents.text: Current validated rollout plan VELA_208-D in the fictional Iris project applies accepted labels to the primary collection after a signed trial decision. The plan covers deployment, not how to run an isolated reversible trial.

documents.title: Synthetic Juniper: revoked credentials
documents.text: Current validated response in the fictional Juniper project: when a credential is revoked, disable its access immediately and retain the revocation event in the audit log. Restoring access requires a newly issued credential; the revoked one cannot be renewed.

documents.title: Synthetic Juniper: expiring credentials
documents.text: Current validated response in the fictional Juniper project: a credential approaching its scheduled expiry may be renewed while it remains valid, provided its owner confirms continued need. This renewal path is unavailable for revoked credentials.

documents.title: Synthetic Juniper: replacement receipt
documents.text: Current validated form ID AMBER:9X-204 in the fictional Juniper project records issuance of a replacement credential. Required fields are old credential handle, new credential handle, issuer, and issuance time. It is a receipt schema, not an access-restoration policy.

documents.title: Synthetic Juniper: renewal receipt
documents.text: Current validated form ID AMBER:9X-240 in the fictional Juniper project records renewal of a still-valid credential. Required fields are credential handle, confirming owner, and revised expiry time. No new credential handle is issued through this form.

documents.title: Synthetic Alder: scheduled handoff appointment
documents.text: Current validated scheduling convention for the fictional Alder project: handoff appointments occupy a reserved calendar slot between two workers. This note describes booking the conversation and says nothing about which actions must appear in an unfinished-work capsule.

documents.title: Synthetic Harbor: cabinet inventory
documents.text: Current validated inventory convention for the fictional Harbor project: cabinet shelves receive sequential location numbers. This note identifies physical packet locations only; it does not determine whether a packet is approved or eligible for publication.
